Clarity.justification: The paper is written with unusual meticulousness about its own limitations and protocol details, which is commendable for transparency but severely harms readability. The abstract alone is 300+ words and contains implementation-level details (e.g., 'selection-split corrected AUROC 0.6092–0.7011 against a pre-registered 0.55 gate') that belong in the results section. The paper reads more like an internal experiment log than a research paper — terms like 'h-e1', 'h-e1-v2', 'A2-v2', 'FR-5.2', 'NFR-6' appear throughout without being standard academic notation. The staged verification design, while intellectually honest, creates a confusing narrative where the reader must constantly track what was measured, what was planned but not measured, and what failed. Section 3.5's discussion of the anchor failure, while interesting, is presented with excessive procedural detail. The core idea — reading logit-lens uncertainty at intermediate layers for hallucination detection — is actually simple and could be communicated much more concisely. The paper would benefit enormously from restructuring to lead with the simple method and results, relegating the protocol forensics to a shorter subsection or appendix.

Novelty.justification: The novelty is incremental. The logit lens is well-established (nostalgebraist 2020, Belrose et al. 2023), and the idea that intermediate layers carry stronger truthfulness signals than the final layer is described by the authors themselves as 'close to consensus' (Orgad et al. 2024). The specific contribution is evaluating standard uncertainty statistics (entropy, max-prob) from logit-lens distributions as detection scores without training a probe — a natural and somewhat obvious combination of existing tools. The adjacent-layer KL divergence as a detection signal is the most novel element, but it is a straightforward extension of DoLa-style layer contrasting from decoding to detection. The protocol-internal validity anchor is presented as a contribution but is essentially good experimental practice (comparing within the same protocol) rather than a methodological innovation. The paper's honest framing as 'existence-tier evidence' appropriately scopes the claims, but this also means the contribution is demonstrating that a natural idea works at a basic level, which is limited novelty for a top venue.

Soundness.justification: There are several significant methodological concerns. First and most critically, ALL reported results are selection-split values — the same data used to select the (layer, signal, direction) tuple is used to evaluate it. The paper acknowledges this repeatedly but still reports these numbers as the main results. The 'corrected AUROC' = max(a, 1-a) with direction selection on the same data introduces substantial optimistic bias, especially when searching over ~90 (layer, signal) combinations per cell. With this many comparisons and no multiple-testing correction, finding something above 0.55 by chance is plausible. The paper provides no confidence intervals, no bootstrap tests, and no multiple-comparison corrections. The thinnest margin (+0.0035 for LLaMA-3/TruthfulQA) is acknowledged as 'within plausible noise,' but even the larger margins could be inflated by selection bias. Second, the class imbalance is severe in some cells (e.g., LLaMA-2/TruthfulQA has 383 positive vs 25 negative cases; LLaMA-3/TruthfulQA has 372 vs 36), which makes AUROC estimates unstable. Third, the test splits were never evaluated, meaning the central claims remain unvalidated. The code appears consistent with the described methodology and the experiment logs support that real models were run, but the fundamental issue is that the evaluation design does not support the strength of the claims made. The paper's own staged design acknowledges this, but publishing existence-tier results without the confirmation tier is premature.

Significance.justification: The practical significance is limited by several factors. The AUROC values (0.61–0.70 on selection splits, likely lower on held-out data) are well below the supervised probe skyline (0.73–0.85) and below what would be needed for practical deployment. The method requires per-model, per-dataset selection of the (layer, signal, direction) tuple, which means labeled data is still needed — just less of it than for probe training. The paper does not demonstrate that the selected tuples transfer across datasets (this was planned but not executed), which would be necessary for practical use. The protocol forensics finding — that six protocol choices moved AUROC by 0.074 — is a useful cautionary note but is not surprising to experienced practitioners. The scope is limited to three 7-8B models and two short-form QA datasets with greedy decoding. The paper explicitly acknowledges the familiarity-vs-truthfulness confound is unaddressed. The most significant potential contribution — adjacent-layer KL as a detection signal — is interesting but demonstrated only at the existence level without held-out validation.

strengths: Exceptional transparency about limitations: the paper is remarkably honest about what it does and does not establish, clearly flagging selection-split bias, single-seed results, and unmeasured tiers. This level of scientific honesty is rare and commendable.

Complete reproducibility infrastructure: the code is well-organized, the experiment logs are detailed, cached results are provided, and the locked test splits enable future confirmation. The implementation includes automated tests and verification checks.

The protocol forensics finding (Section 5.4) is a genuinely useful contribution to the community, demonstrating concretely how protocol choices affect weak-signal AUROC and motivating within-protocol comparisons.
The adjacent-layer KL divergence as a detection signal is a reasonable novel contribution that connects the DoLa/decoding-contrast literature to the detection literature.
weaknesses: No held-out evaluation: all reported AUROCs are computed on the same data used for model selection (layer, signal, direction), with no multiple-testing correction across ~90 comparisons per cell. The locked test splits were never evaluated, making the central claims unvalidated. This is the most critical weakness.

Modest effect sizes that may not survive proper evaluation: the best selection-split AUROCs (0.61–0.70) are well below supervised methods and may shrink substantially on held-out data given the selection bias. One margin is +0.0035, and even larger margins lack confidence intervals.
Severe class imbalance in several cells (e.g., 383:25 in LLaMA-2/TruthfulQA) makes AUROC estimates unreliable, yet no stratified analysis or alternative metrics are provided.

The paper is excessively long and reads like an internal experiment log rather than a research paper, with implementation-level details (cache management, session interruptions, file paths) that obscure the core contribution.
Limited scope: only three 7-8B models from one architectural lineage, two QA datasets, greedy decoding only, and the familiarity-vs-truthfulness confound is explicitly unaddressed.
